- Universe: EPA's amendments as listed in Doc 6 L126: August 5, 2016; July 30, 2018; August 28, 2020; November 12, 2020; May 8, 2024; November 8, 2024; February 10, 2026. The last is the latest. Doc 2 L127 lists the first six only.
- Necessity: Doc 2 is the only source of August 19, 2022 (grep: D02 L278 only). February 10, 2026 is printed in Doc 3 L119, Doc 4 L122, Doc 5 L127 and Doc 6 L126 and nowhere in Doc 2 (grep), so those four are grouped as alternatives, anchored on Doc 6 because it is the September 2026 document the question's date points to. Without that group the newest listed amendment is November 8, 2024 and the count is 812.
- Selected-lever checks: Same series, right edition: Doc 2's own list gives 2024-11-08, 812 days; the 2026 editions give 1,271. Calculate across documents: one date from Doc 2, one from Doc 6, one day count. No which-items decoy applies.
- Targeted failure modes: mode 1 (Wrong year or edition / Uses the wrong period or date): Doc 2 L127 ends at November 8, 2024 -> 812 days. Recomputed 2026-10-10. Considered and not declared: counting from Wyoming's December 14, 2020 federal cutoff (D02 L278) instead of the effective date -> 1,884 days, which "chapter 18 took effect" rules out; Wyoming's 1990 and 1975 rules (L278) are not chapter 18.
- Calculation verification: python 2026-10-10 (caller): date(2026,2,10) - date(2022,8,19) = 1,271 days; date(2025,8,19) - date(2022,8,19) = 1,096; date(2026,2,10) - date(2025,8,19) = 175; date(2025,8,19) + 180 days = 2026-02-15, 5 days after February 10; wrong routes 812 and 1,884. Elapsed days (the later date minus the earlier), the convention of "how many days after".
- Semantic/ID/overview probes: no document prints 1,271 or any interval between a State rule and a federal amendment. The page overview lists Doc 2's "August 19, 2022" among its dates and no amendment date. Shortest route: Doc 2 L278, any 2026 proposal's amendment list, one day count.

sections.question: As of September 2026, how many days after Wyoming's Solid Waste Rules chapter 18 took effect did EPA last amend the federal coal-ash regulations?
sections.reasoning:
Step 1. Source input (Doc 2, Wyoming CCR Regulations): Wyoming's coal ash rules are Solid Waste Rules chapter 18, and "chapter 18 became effective on August 19, 2022".
Step 2. Source input (Doc 6, Background): Doc 6 was published on September 11, 2026 and lists every amendment EPA has made to the federal coal ash regulations. The list ends with "February 10, 2026 (91 FR 5806)", so that is the latest amendment as of September 2026.
Step 3. Source input (Doc 2, Background): Doc 2 was published on September 2, 2025, and its own list of amendments ends with "November 8, 2024 (89 FR 88650)". It predates the amendment in Step 2, so its list is not the latest one.
Step 4. Calculation (Doc 2 and Doc 6): twelve thirty-day months, in days: 12 × 30 = 360.
Step 5. Calculation (Doc 2 and Doc 6): a common year is five days longer than that: 360 + 5 = 365.
Step 6. Calculation (Doc 2 and Doc 6): from August 19, 2022 to August 19, 2025 is 3 years, which at a common year's length is, in days: 365 × 3 = 1,095.
Step 7. Calculation (Doc 2 and Doc 6): one of those years holds a leap day (February 2024), which adds a day: 1,095 + 1 = 1,096.
Step 8. Calculation (Doc 2 and Doc 6): 180 days after August 19, 2025 falls 5 days after February 10, 2026, so the remaining stretch in days is: 180 - 5 = 175.
Step 9. Final answer (Doc 2 and Doc 6): days from chapter 18 taking effect to EPA's latest amendment: 1,096 + 175 = 1,271.
sections.targeted failure modes:
### Failure mode 1
Trap: Wrong year or edition
How a careless solver fails: Uses the wrong period or date

Why these are traps: Wrong year or edition: Doc 2, the September 2025 Wyoming proposal, lists EPA's amendments only through November 8, 2024; using it gives 812 days. Doc 6, published September 11, 2026, lists a later amendment, February 10, 2026, so the count from August 19, 2022 is 1,271 days.
